text:
sara_support: FYI @devon_eng @alia_ml — Finovate says their assistant's replies got noticeably shorter and a bit more 'blunt' after the v4 rollout. Customer provided before/after examples and a repro curl.

jamal_support: ugh. any error logs or request ids? severity? :thinking_face:

sara_support: Only one customer so far, high-value pilot. They flagged reduced explanatory content and fewer follow-up q's. Sent samples below. request_id: req_fino_20260316_01.

sara_support: BEFORE (v3.2):
```
User: "How can I lower my monthly fees?"
Assistant: "You can save by reviewing your subscription plan and turning off auto-renew. If you'd like, I can check your billing history and suggest specific changes or discounts based on your usage. Would you like me to look into that now?"
```

sara_support: AFTER (v4.0):
```
User: "How can I lower my monthly fees?"
Assistant: "Check your plan settings and disable auto-renew."
```

jamal_support: that's subtle but definitely a UX regression. do we have the exact API payload they used?

sara_support: yes — customer sent this (redacted token):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v4","prompt":"User: \"How can I lower my monthly fees?\"\nAssistant:","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":120}'
```

sara_support: They said switching model param back to "redwood-v3.2" in their test restored the longer replies.

devon_eng: @alia_ml can you check if any generation defaults changed in v4 (stop sequences, max_new_tokens truncation, or decoding samplers)?

alia_ml: on it. also checking whether the model's finetune/llm-prompting target changed — sometimes training objectives bias conciseness.

deploy-bot: Deployment complete: redwood-v4 rollout to prod cluster eu-west-1 at 1975399000. No automatic rollback triggered.

devon_eng: sara — can you share sample of full request headers + content-length and the exact response tokens? need to rule out truncation via content-length or streaming last-chunk drop.

jamal_support: I asked the customer to run one more test with temp=0.7 and top_p=0.95 to see if stochasticity returns more elaboration. waiting on reply. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alia_ml: quick note: v4 changed tokenizer mapping for a few frequent phrases — could compress longer explanations into fewer tokens, but that would usually produce longer or same-length responses, not shorter. Still investigating.

devon_eng: also comparing quantization/kernels between v3.2 and v4 on serving side. some kernel reorderings can change beam/greedy stepping at edge cases.

sara_support: customer ran temp=0.7 test — got slightly longer replies but still more concise than v3.2 baseline. They uploaded a zipped repro bundle: https://fino-files.internal/req_fino_20260316_01.zip

alia_ml: grabbing the bundle and launching regression harness (eval-run: concise_regression_v4). Will run with their prompt set + our standard explainability prompt bank.

devon_eng: I'll diff the model configs and serving flags (batching windows, max_tokens cap). tagging eng-runtime.

alia_ml: if we confirm a behavior shift, options: patch model finetune, adjust default decoding settings for v4, or add a per-customer routing rule to v3.2 until fix. Which is preferable for Finovate?

jamal_support: customer prefers no downtime; they'd accept a temporary routing to v3.2 for their tenant while we diagnose.

devon_eng: can do a tenant-route if SRE ok. @eng-sre — can we route finovate-org-id to redwood-v3.2 in eu-west-1 as a quick mitigation?

deploy-bot: Canary traffic rules can be updated via console. Patch to routing table requires a 10m deploy window and config review.

alia_ml: starting local eval now; will post summary + metric diffs (avg_tokens, explainability_score, followup-prompt-rate).

devon_eng: created eng-ml ticket RID-2026 to track root cause and plan. I'll link logs and kernel diffs.

sara_support: thanks everyone. keeping Finovate in the loop — I'll offer v3.2 routing as short-term option. please flag ETA for mitigation so I can update customer.

alia_ml: rough ETA 6-12 hours for initial eval results. will update thread. :white_check_mark:

jamal_support: noted, I'll push a status update to the customer after devon confirms routing feasibility.

devon_eng: posting follow-up: if routing approved, I can have policy live in ~30m after config-change window.

alia_ml: initial evals show a 22% drop in mean token count and a 0.18 drop in our explainability score vs v3.2 on Finovate prompt set. saving full report to the ticket.

sara_support: solid — thanks. I'll standby for the routing window then update customer.

devon_eng: switching to eng-ml sync. will update ticket RID-2026 when we have root cause.

alia_ml: TL;DR: behavioral drift confirmed; not API error/latency. next steps: deeper model-level repro, decide hotfix vs routing.

sara_support: closing loop — customer accepted temporary routing to v3.2. I'll note rollback duration and follow-up with product for longer-term plan.
